problems.title: Packing candy bags
problems.statement: You have {{n}} identical fruit candies to distribute into {{k}} distinct gift bags. Bags are allowed to remain empty. In how many different ways can the candies be distributed?

answer.prompt: Number of ways to distribute the candies

common_wrong.feedback: To divide items into {{k}} bags, you need only {{k}}-1 dividers, not {{k}}.
That formula treats the candies as distinct. Because the candies are identical, swapping two candies between bags does not create a new arrangement.
Dividers are identical, so their order relative to each other does not matter.

slot_mistakes.feedback: Dividing candies among {{k}} bags requires {{k}}-1 dividers.

help_steps.title: Draw one way as a picture
help_steps.text: Write the $n$ candies as stars in a row and cut the row into $k$ bags with $k-1$ bars, like ●● | ● | ●●●. Every picture is one way to share, and every way gives one picture.

help_steps.title: Count the pictures
help_steps.text: The row has $n + k - 1$ symbols. Choosing which $k - 1$ of them are bars decides the whole picture. Now fill in the numbers.

solution.title: Count symbols in stars and bars
solution.explanation: Represent the {{n}} identical candies as stars and use {{k}}-1 dividers to partition them into {{k}} distinct bags, giving {{n}}+{{k}}-1 total symbols.

solution.title: Choose divider positions
solution.explanation: From the {{n}}+{{k}}-1 symbol positions, choose {{k}}-1 positions for the dividers.

visual.legend: ● = a candy, | = a divider between bags

problems.twist: every bag gets at least one candy
problems.title: No empty candy bags
problems.statement: You have {{n}} identical fruit candies to distribute into {{k}} distinct gift bags, but every bag must receive at least one candy. In how many different ways can the candies be distributed?

answer.prompt: Number of ways to distribute the candies

common_wrong.feedback: That allows bags to be empty. Here, every bag must receive at least one candy.
There are {{n}}-1 spaces between consecutive candies to place {{k}}-1 dividers.
All dividers are identical, so their order does not create new distributions.

help_steps.title: Give every bag one candy first
help_steps.text: That uses $k$ candies and makes sure no bag is empty. The other $n - k$ candies can go anywhere.

help_steps.title: Share the rest with stars and bars
help_steps.text: Now $n - k$ candies go into $k$ bags, where a bag may get none. That's $n - k + k - 1 = n - 1$ symbols with $k - 1$ bars. Now fill in the numbers.

solution.title: Line up candies and locate gaps
solution.explanation: Lining up the {{n}} candies creates {{n}}-1 internal gaps between adjacent candies.

solution.title: Place dividers in distinct gaps
solution.explanation: Placing at most one divider per gap ensures no bag is empty, so choose {{k}}-1 gaps out of {{n}}-1.

visual.legend: ● = a candy, | = a divider between bags

problems.twist: one specific bag receives a minimum amount
problems.title: Special bag minimum
problems.statement: You have {{n}} identical fruit candies to distribute into {{k}} distinct gift bags. A designated gold bag must receive at least {{m}} candies, while the other bags may receive any number (including zero). In how many different ways can the candies be distributed?

answer.prompt: Number of ways to distribute the candies

common_wrong.feedback: This counts all distributions without enforcing that the gold bag gets at least {{m}} candies.
The {{n}}-{{m}} remaining candies can go into any of the {{k}} bags, so the number of positions is ({{n}}-{{m}})+{{k}}-1.
Placing identical dividers into available positions is an unordered choice.

help_steps.title: Fill the gold bag's minimum first
help_steps.text: Put $m$ candies in the gold bag straight away. That leaves $n - m$ candies with no rules at all.

help_steps.title: Share the rest with stars and bars
help_steps.text: Now $n - m$ candies go into $k$ bags, where a bag may get none: $n - m + k - 1$ symbols with $k - 1$ bars. Now fill in the numbers.

solution.title: Pre-assign candies to the gold bag
solution.explanation: Place {{m}} candies into the gold bag first, leaving {{n}}-{{m}} candies to distribute freely among all {{k}} bags.

solution.title: Distribute the remaining candies
solution.explanation: Apply standard stars and bars to place {{n}}-{{m}} identical candies into {{k}} bags with {{k}}-1 dividers.
